summary: The payment failures reported by customers are caused by an expired mTLS client certificate on the payment-service -> bank-partner-api hop (H1, confidence 0.68): the certificate presented by payment-service reached notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z, and from the first outbound call at 12:15:27Z every bank call is rejected at the TLS handshake, driving bank_api_error_rate to exactly 100% and payment_success_rate from ~99% to ~2.5% while the 5xx error_rate panel stays flat (failures are returned as PENDING_RETRY, not errors). The failure mode is unambiguous — decomposition shows 0 timeout and 0 5xx signatures and only TLS-handshake/expired-certificate errors — which rules out the timeout config change (H3) and the partner-5xx/degradation reading (H2), and ledger-db, db_pool, kafka-facing and api-gateway signals are all flat at onset, ruling out H4/H5. Two premises remain unverifiable and cap confidence: whether CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal is our own credential or partner-issued (no cert/secret store is queryable — the root-cause statement should therefore not claim ownership), and whether the ~40 support tickets map to this exact failure (no ticket telemetry exists). The defect and its impact are identical under either ownership reading, and the crit

ranked_hypotheses.title: Expired client mTLS certificate on the payment-service -> bank-partner-api hop
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The mTLS client certificate presented by payment-service on calls to bank-partner-api (CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal, notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z) became invalid at 12:15:00Z. From the next outbound call at 12:15:27Z every bank call is rejected at the TLS handshake ('remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)'), so transfers are marked PENDING_RETRY and returned as non-error responses — payment_success_rate collapses to ~2.5%, bank_api_error_rate hits exactly 100%, latency falls (fast handshake reject), while the 5xx error_rate panel stays flat. Framing caveat per critique: whether this cert is minted/rotated BY us or is a partner-issued credential is NOT verified; the defect is an expired credential on the handshake, and the failure mechanism/impact is the same either way.

causal_chain.claim: The client certificate used by payment-service to call bank-partner-api reaches notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z; a cert-watcher already warned 'expires in 25 minutes' at 11:50:26Z
The next outbound call at 12:15:27Z is rejected: 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' / 'remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45)', with no timeout or 5xx signature anywhere
All outbound bank calls now fail, so bank_api_error_rate steps from ~0.2% to exactly 100% and payment_success_rate collapses ~97 points, both first deviating in the 12:15 bucket
Failures are caught and recorded as 'marked PENDING_RETRY' (non-error responses), so the 5xx error_rate panel never moves and latency_p99 DROPS as handshakes fail fast

The failure is continuous and customer-scale through the window: ~140 PENDING_RETRY entries at ~1.4/min from 12:15:27Z to 13:57:46Z, consistent with the ~40 tickets reported in the last 15 minutes at 12:32Z
The reporter's symptom (payment failures, green error dashboard) is the direct consequence of steps 2-5 on the transfer route

assumptions: The notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z certificate is a credential on the payment-service call path (client-side of our identity as logged); whether we issue/rotate it or the partner does is UNVERIFIED — no cert/secret store was queryable. H1's framing must not claim ownership; H1 and H2 differ mainly on this unresolved premise.

The ~40 support tickets map to this exact bank-call failure rather than a distinct client-app issue — the ticket system has no telemetry (F19), so the link rests on matching rate/timing, not ticket content.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Bank partner came to reject our mTLS handshake (partner-side certificate/trust failure) — reporter's external-boundary suspicion, refined
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The failure sits on the bank partner side: because bank-partner-api has no telemetry, a partner-side certificate/trust change (e.g. their CA rotating or the credentials they accept for CN=payments-client... changing) would surface to us exactly as a TLS handshake rejection and 100% bank_api_error_rate, with payment-service degrading gracefully into PENDING_RETRY — the same symptom shape as HIST-105. This differs from the reporter's raw 'bank outage' framing only in mechanism (handshake/cert trust, not 5xx/timeout).

causal_chain.claim: bank-partner-api (external, has_telemetry=false) begins rejecting our mTLS handshake or otherwise failing around 12:15Z — unobservable directly
payment-service outbound bank calls fail, driving bank_api_error_rate to exactly 100% and payment_success_rate to ~2.5%
Graceful degradation marks transfers PENDING_RETRY, keeping the 5xx error_rate green while success collapses
Precedent HIST-105 (2025-11-19, bank partner 5xx for 40 min) shows this symptom shape from a partner-side cause

assumptions: The 'expired certificate (alert 45)' is generated by our client rejecting the server/its own expired cert, which is what alert 45 typically means — this makes a pure partner-side cause hard to sustain
A partner-side change would produce a TLS cert-expiry alert rather than timeouts/5xx (not the usual signature of a partner degradation)

ranked_hypotheses.title: bank.api.timeout_ms config change (3000->5000) at 11:20Z caused the failures
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The only config change in the window — payment-service bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 ms at 11:20Z — introduced the bank-call failures with a delayed 12:15Z onset.

causal_chain.claim: Config change raises bank API timeout 3000->5000 ms on payment-service at 11:20Z
The changed timeout causes bank calls to fail/hang, producing transfer failures
Failures surface as bank_api_error_rate 100% and payment_success_rate collapse

assumptions: None surviving — no mechanism links a timeout increase to a TLS cert-expiry alert
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Mechanically impossible for a timeout increase to produce TLS 'expired certificate (alert 45)' rejections (F27/F28: 0 timeout and 0 5xx signature matches). The 55-minute gap is now shown real, not a masking artifact: metrics were flat in finer 60s buckets through 11:20 and up to 12:14 (success 98.76 avg at the 11:20 bucket; bank error 0.20; fully normal 12:12-12:14), with no bank-error or timeout warnings between the 11:20Z change and the 12:15Z collapse (F25, F29, F30). A timeout change would surface as slow calls/timeouts and/or a latency RISE; latency instead DROPPED (F11).

ranked_hypotheses.title: settlement-service v1.9.0 (10:30Z) co-tenant effect via shared ledger-db or shared kafka backlog
ranked_hypotheses.statement: settlement-service v1.9.0 (new CSV exporter, 10:30Z) loaded the shared ledger-db or backed up shared kafka, degrading the payment transfer path while payment-service's own error rate stayed green.

causal_chain.claim: settlement-service v1.9.0 deploys at 10:30Z with a new CSV exporter
The exporter consumes shared ledger-db capacity and/or backs up the shared kafka queue
Payment transfer path degrades through the shared resources, failing transfers while HTTP errors stay green

assumptions: settlement-service v1.9.0 increased load on ledger-db or kafka (no metric evidence obtained)
ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Contradicted on mechanism and scope: the observed failure localises to the payment-service -> bank-partner-api TLS handshake (F7/F9/F28), which a DB/queue contention problem cannot produce (it would not yield an exact 100% bank_api_error_rate or a 'tls: expired certificate' alert). ledger-db shows no degradation (F13 slow_queries flat through the incident, only spike 21 min BEFORE onset; F14 replication_lag stable 35-44ms; F15 db_pool flat ~8). Onset would track the 10:30Z deploy, but both series are flat through 10:30 and 11:20 and only deviate at 12:15 (F25, F29). Kafka consumer-lag was never enumerated, so a co-tenant contribution cannot be fully excluded, but no positive co-tenant signal exists.

ranked_hypotheses.title: Ledger-db / DB connection-pool exhaustion on the transfer path
ranked_hypotheses.statement: The transfer path fails because ledger-db is slow or the payment-service DB pool is exhausted, causing ledger writes to fail or hang while the aggregate HTTP error panel stays green.

causal_chain.claim: ledger-db slow queries or replication stall begins around 12:15Z
payment-service DB pool saturates, blocking transfer writes
Transfers fail in a way not surfacing as 5xx

ranked_hypotheses.rejection_reason: Directly contradicted by F13 (ledger-db slow_queries flat ~0.77-1.15 through the incident; only spike at 11:54Z, 21 min BEFORE onset), F14 (replication_lag stable 35-44ms), F15 (payment-service db_pool_in_use flat ~8, no step at 12:15), and by F7/F9 which localise the failure to the mTLS/TLS handshake to bank-partner-api, not the DB.

data_gaps: No telemetry/metric queries were made against payment-service, settlement-service, ledger-db, kafka or bank-partner-api in this round (budget spent on change history and dependency mapping), so I cannot say whether any metric moved at the 11:20Z config change or the 10:30Z deployment.
bank-partner-api is external with has_telemetry=false, so no metrics or logs exist for the bank rail itself.

Two historical-incident searches for 'payments fail for customers but dashboard green' and 'silent failure missing telemetry dashboard green payment' returned count=0; only the bank-rail query matched.

Could not query logs or metrics for bank-partner-api: the tool returned not_found, stating "'bank-partner-api' is an external dependency: we have no logs/metrics for it. Observe it through its callers" (callers: payment-service).

Tool-call budget was exhausted before I could run per-endpoint/per-route error rates, 5xx-vs-4xx breakdown, timeout/retry counters, and a request_rate check; the only retry evidence captured is one WARN 'retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset' at 12:04:22Z.
No metrics were checked for other services in the transfer flow (e.g. ledger/account/wallet services) beyond payment-service and the external bank-partner-api.

payment-service exposes no timeout_rate, connection_errors, or DNS/TLS-specific metric (query returned not_found listing the 9 available metrics); the granular per-failure-mode breakdown of the bank rail (timeouts vs cert rejection vs connection refused) could not be measured and had to be inferred from bank_api_error_rate=100% plus the ERROR log signature.

No transfer-queue consumer-lag or queue-depth metric could be enumerated for kafka/settlement-service/notification-service within the remaining budget; the queue hop's health during 12:15-13:59 is unverified.

The active client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal and its notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z could only be seen in payment-service ERROR logs; no certificate-validity or secret/config telemetry was queryable.
No support/helpdesk/ticketing service exists in telemetry (query_logs for 'support-service' and 'helpdesk-service' both returned not_found; known_services contains no CRM/ticket component).

email-provider (customer-facing failure-notification fan-out) is an external dependency with no logs or metrics; notification-service shows 0 WARN+ entries so its fan-out could not be confirmed either.
PENDING_RETRY query was truncated (returned 20 of total_matched 140), so the 140 count is a floor and the full per-minute distribution of failing payments was not enumerated.

payment-service exposes no timeout/connection/TLS failure-counter metric (only bank_api_error_rate plus generic ones), so the timeout-vs-TLS-vs-5xx split cannot be computed from a counter or histogram; the decomposition rests on log-signature counts (0 timeout, 0 5xx, 44 TLS entries) rather than on metric values.

bank-partner-api (external bank rail) has has_telemetry=false, so no partner-side telemetry (their 5xx rate, timeout rate, response codes) could be queried directly; partner health is inferred only from the absence of '5xx' matches in payment-service logs.

Log queries were run per-pattern ('timeout', '5xx') with a contains filter over a single service; I did not enumerate the full unfiltered WARN/ERROR pattern inventory of other services (settlement-service, kafka consumers) in 10:30-12:20Z, so a co-tenant signal invisible in payment-service cannot be excluded.

No certificate-store / secret-manager / keystore tool was available: get_config_changes only exposes application config keys, and queries scoped to bank-partner-api and payment-service returned only the timeout_ms key. The entry for CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal could not be read from any store.

No scheduled-job / cron / rotation-run history tool was available, so the question 'did the payment-service->bank-partner-api rotation run, fail, or get skipped around 12:15Z' could not be answered directly; the empty config-change record is only weak negative evidence.

The final depth-3 get_service_dependencies call for payment-service returned {"ok": false, "error": {"type": "budget_exhausted"}} and was never executed (only the depth-2 graph was already known from the team).

findings.statement: Only one deployment occurred across all services in the window 2026-04-01T00:00Z through 2026-04-02T13:59Z: settlement-service v1.9.0 at 2026-04-02T10:30:00Z by ci-bot ("Batch settlement report export", change "new CSV exporter"), status live, not rolled back. No deployment touched payment-service in the window.

Only one config change occurred across all services in the window: payment-service key bank.api.timeout_ms changed from 3000 to 5000 ms at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by author p.nair, described as "Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory". This is a payment-service change ~72 minutes before the 12:32Z report.

refs.quote: Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory

findings.statement: payment-service dependency graph: outbound edges are payment-service -> ledger-db (kind db), payment-service -> bank-partner-api (kind external, has_telemetry=false), payment-service -> kafka (kind queue-produce); inbound edge api-gateway -> payment-service (http). The external bank rail adapter has NO telemetry.

ledger-db is a SHARED postgres used by four services: order-service, portfolio-service, payment-service and settlement-service all write/read it (edges to ledger-db kind db). Settlement-service is thus a co-tenant of the ledger that payment-service depends on.

kafka is a SHARED queue: payment-service and order-service produce (queue-produce) while settlement-service and notification-service consume (queue-consume). A consumer slowdown or backlog on settlement-service can therefore affect the transfer flow without showing in payment-service's own error rate.

Historical precedent for the "payment failures with normal/failed dashboard" shape: HIST-105 (2025-11-19) 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' on payment-service — root cause 'Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes (their incident)', category dependency_failure, resolution 'Waited for partner; queued retries'. This is a lead, not evidence about the current incident.

refs.quote: Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes

findings.statement: payment-service received ERROR logs on the transfer path starting 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z: 'payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected', then 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z'. 313 ERROR-level entries matched, first 12:15:27Z, last 13:58:39Z.

refs.quote: payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected

findings.statement: The metric that shows the failure is payment_success_rate, which collapses from ~99% (avg 98.62-99.81 across 11:45-12:09) to ~2.5% at the 12:15 bucket (avg 2.51, max 2.99) and stays ~2-2.8% through 13:57 — a sustained ~97 point drop coincident with the 12:15:27Z log onset.
bank_api_error_rate on payment-service jumps from ~0.2% (flat 11:45-12:09) to exactly 100.0 for every bucket from 12:15 onward through 13:57, confirming the bank call path is entirely failing.

The aggregate HTTP error_rate panel (5xx % of requests) stays flat and low throughout, between 0.17 and 0.32% (max 0.32) across all buckets 11:45-13:57, with no change at 12:15 — confirming the incident is invisible to the 5xx error-rate panel even though transfers are failing 100%.

latency_p99_ms on payment-service DROPS rather than rises at onset — from ~318-341ms (11:45-12:09) to ~135-150ms (12:15-13:57) — consistent with bank calls failing fast (TLS handshake reject) instead of completing, so latency signals cannot be used to detect this incident.

Failures on the transfer path are logged at ERROR level (not silent) with two dominant signature patterns, but the app classifies them as successful responses ('marked PENDING_RETRY'), which explains why the 5xx error_rate panel stays green.

bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert <n>); our client cert CN=payments-

findings.statement: ledger-db shows no degradation at or after the 12:15Z onset: slow_queries_per_min is flat (~0.77-1.15 avg per bucket for every bucket from 12:12 onward), and its only spike (avg 5.4, max 9.63) is at 11:54Z, ~21 minutes BEFORE the incident began, so the DB is not failing during the incident window.

ledger-db replication_lag_ms is completely stable across the whole window (min 35.27, max 44.34, mean 39.7 ms; bucket avgs 38.85-40.59 for 11:45-13:51), showing no ledger write/replication stall coincident with the 12:15Z failure onset.

payment-service db_pool_in_use is flat at ~8 connections (mean 7.99, min 7.19, max 8.95) for every bucket from 11:45 through 13:51, with no step at 12:15 — the service did not run out of DB connections and there is no DB-saturation signature on the transfer path.

api-gateway has 0 ERROR-level log entries in 2026-04-02T12:00:00Z-13:59:00Z (total_matched 0, truncated false, empty top_patterns), so the client/edge component in front of payment-service logs no errors at all during the failure window; the only server-side error evidence is inside payment-service.

api-gateway request_rate stays flat (~1120-1453 req/s, mean 1267.82) across 11:45-13:51 including the 12:15-13:57 failure period, so inbound client traffic volume did not change when transfers started failing — the failures are not a client-side traffic artifact.

payment-service exposes only 9 metrics (bank_api_error_rate, cpu_pct, db_pool_in_use, error_rate, latency_p99_ms, memory_pct, payment_success_rate, request_rate, restarts): there is NO timeout_rate, NO connection_errors, and NO DNS/TLS metric, so the outbound bank-rail hop can only be characterised through bank_api_error_rate (already 100%) and the mTLS/expired-certificate log signature — granular timeout vs TLS-failure breakdown is unavailable.

No support/helpdesk ticket telemetry exists: querying 'support-service' and 'helpdesk-service' returns not_found, and the known_services list contains no ticket/CRM component (only api-gateway, auth-service, order-service, portfolio-service, pricing-engine, market-data-service, payment-service, settlement-service, notification-service, exchange-gateway, ledger-db, user-db, redis-cache, kafka, exchange-api, bank-partner-api, kyc-provider, email-provider). The customer-visible link can only be inferred from the failing route's error text, not from ticket data.

The failing transfer path emits exactly one dominant ERROR signature, 140 matches of 'payment <n> marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' between first_match 2026-04-02T12:15:27Z and last_match 2026-04-02T13:57:46Z (truncated=true, so 140 is a floor), each carrying a distinct payment id (e.g. 45f233b6 at 12:15:27Z, 7b4c31a9 at 12:16:13Z, 03ba104b at 12:17:57Z). This is the 'pending retry' state referenced in the task, produced continuously through the window.

refs.quote: payment 45f233b6 marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected
payment 03ba104b marked PENDING_RETRY: mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected

findings.statement: PENDING_RETRY failures are frequent and customer-scale in the ticket window: 140 recorded in the trailing ~102 minutes from 12:15:27Z, i.e. roughly 1.4 per minute sustained, and they continue well past the 12:32Z report (last at 13:57:46Z) — consistent with ~40 support tickets in the last ~15 minutes at report time rather than a short burst.

The failing route traffic volume is unchanged: payment-service request_rate is flat at ~90-110 req/s across 12:00-13:59 (bucket avgs 98.48-101.67, overall mean 100.62, missing_points 0), so requests keep arriving and are failing on the bank leg rather than the endpoint being called less.

No client-app/edge-side failure signature exists in telemetry: api-gateway logs matching '/transfer' in 12:00-13:59Z return total_matched 0 (truncated false), and notification-service shows 0 WARN+ entries in the same window, so the client-facing edge and notification path record no errors of their own. There is no evidence pointing at a distinct client-app error signature in the observability data.

email-provider (the notification fan-out dependency customers would receive transfer-failure mail from) is an external dependency with no telemetry: the query returns not_found with message that it must be observed through its caller notification-service, which itself logged no WARN+ entries.

refs.quote: 'email-provider' is an external dependency: we have no logs/metrics for it

findings.statement: payment_success_rate and bank_api_error_rate both stay at baseline through the 12:14 bucket and step to failure in the 12:15 bucket, i.e. onset is between 12:14 and 12:15Z. In 60s buckets: payment_success_rate = 99.68 (12:14) then 2.18 (12:15), 2.99 (12:16); bank_api_error_rate = 0.21 (12:14) then exactly 100.0 for every bucket 12:15-12:30. Neither series shows any change at 11:20Z (success 98.76 avg at 11:20 bucket; bank error 0.2) nor at 10:30Z.

The 240s-bucket view shows partial degradation in the 12:12 bucket (payment_success_rate avg 75.34, bank_api_error_rate avg 25.15, max 100) which is the 12:15Z onset diluted by the 12:12-12:15 sub-interval; in 60s buckets the 12:12-12:14 buckets are fully normal (100.0, 99.52, 99.68 / 0.19, 0.20, 0.21). The FIRST deviating bucket is therefore 12:15 (2.18%), not 12:12 — the coarse bucket makes onset look ~3 min earlier than it was.

Failure-mode decomposition of bank_api_error_rate=100%: in 2026-04-02T11:00:00Z-12:30:00Z payment-service has 44 ERROR entries, all in exactly two patterns — 'mTLS handshake with bank-partner-api rejected' (21) first seen 12:15:27Z and 'bank-partner-api call failed: remote error: tls: expired certificate (alert 45); our client cert CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z' (23). There is no timeout or 5xx signature among them.

findings.statement: Timeout-mode contribution is exactly zero: a log search on 'timeout' for payment-service over 2026-04-02T10:00:00Z-13:59:00Z matches 0 entries (total_matched 0, truncated false), and a search on '5xx' over the same window also matches 0 entries. Neither raised-timeout symptoms (expected if the 3000->5000ms change at 11:20Z were the cause) nor partner 5xx rejections are present, so the 100% bank_api_error_rate is TLS-handshake rejection, not timeouts and not partner 5xx.

The first deviating bucket (12:15) is preceded by a flat pre-onset baseline in finer data, so the onset is NOT an artifact of post-onset-only data: 12:08-12:14 buckets exist and read 99.21/98.47/98.63/99.22/100.0/99.52/99.68 (success) and 0.19-0.22 (bank error), and the 240s series extends back to 10:00Z with success 98.65-99.73 and bank error 0.18-0.22 for every bucket 10:00-12:08.

On the pre-onset transfer path the only bank-related warnings are benign: 3 WARN entries in 11:15-12:15Z, two 'retrying idempotent request (attempt 2) after connection reset' at 11:24:11Z and 12:04:22Z, and one 'cert-watcher: client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)' at 11:50:26Z. No elevated bank-error or timeout warnings appear between the 11:20Z config change and the 12:15Z collapse.

refs.quote: {"ts":"2026-04-02T11:50:26Z","level":"WARN","message":"cert-watcher: client certificate CN=payments-client.orangeinvest.internal expires in 25 minutes (notAfter=2026-04-02T12:15:00Z)"}

findings.statement: The only config change across all services in 2026-04-01T00:00Z-2026-04-02T13:59Z is cfg-2502: payment-service key bank.api.timeout_ms 3000->5000 at 2026-04-02T11:20:00Z by p.nair ('Raise bank API timeout after partner advisory'). No config entry references a certificate, secret, keystore or rotation key for the payment-service->bank-partner-api mTLS path; extending the search back to 2026-01-01 and querying bank-partner-api still returns only cfg-2502 and an empty set respectively.

No deployment at all touched payment-service in the incident window (count 0), so the 12:15Z credential expiry was not accompanied by any payment-service release that could have shipped a new cert or broken the rotation job.

There is a direct precedent for this failure shape: HIST-106 (2025-06-30) 'Settlement mTLS certificate expired' on settlement-service, category credential_expiry, root cause 'Client certificate expired; no renewal automation', resolution 'Issued new cert; added expiry alert'. This is a lead about the missing-rotation class of cause, not evidence about the current incident.

HIST-105 (2025-11-19) 'Payment failures: bank partner API outage' on payment-service is a dependency_failure on the partner side, i.e. the same symptom (payment failures, bank api errors) with a different, external cause - which is why an expired-our-own-certificate cause in 2026 cannot be inferred from symptom similarity alone.

refs.quote: "root_cause":"Bank partner API returned 5xx for 40 minutes (their incident)"

findings.statement: The call direction is payment-service (caller, owner 'payments', has_telemetry true) -> bank-partner-api (external, owner 'vendor', has_telemetry false). The failing side presents CN=payments-client..., i.e. the client certificate of the calling component, which points to payment-service as the credential owner and to the credential being minted for our client identity - but the toolset does not contain the certificate/secret entry that would confirm the issuer.
